subject: Post-call: OrionHealth SDK auth & model-routing runbook
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
To: Ashley Kim <ashley.kim@orionhealth.com>, Devon Park <devon.park@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: OrionHealth SDK auth & model-routing runbook

Thanks for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum.

Summary of needs (from today’s discovery)
- Low-latency patient-facing triage endpoints (~100ms p95 target) in US-East region.
- Embeddings index for 6 months of clinical content (approx 1.2M segments) for semantic search + reranker.
- Strict data residency (US) + per-tenant audit logs.
- Auth: prefer OIDC SSO for console; want server-to-server auth for API (service account + mTLS option).
- Tooling/structured output: want structured discharge summaries from the model + ability to call internal tools for scheduling.

Proposed technical approach (high-level)
1) SDK & auth: we’ll deliver an SDK quickstart that supports service-account keys and mTLS sample. If you want OIDC for console access we can map to SAML/Okta via our SSO integration.
2) Routing & policies: we recommend primary routing to the lowest-cost compatible variant that meets latency SLO (e.g., quantized LLM variant in US-East for short responses, higher-capacity variant for long-form summaries). Fallback chain: low-cost -> standard -> high-accuracy with automatic throttled fallback for bursts.
3) Embeddings + reranker: batch upsert pipeline to our embeddings service (S3 -> Redwood ingestion). Reranker lives as a secondary scoring step; can be triggered via structured tool call in the SDK.
4) Structured output / tool calling: we’ll provide an example tool-handler that turns model JSON output into a calendar-create call to your scheduling service.

Immediate asks from OrionHealth
- Can you share a sample of the clinical segments (anonymized) or an S3 read-only test bucket?
- Which IdP (Okta/Azure) for SSO?
- Any hard latency SLA beyond the p95 target?

Next steps / timeline
- I’ll send a short runbook and SDK quickstart tomorrow (attachments).
- Dev sync to scope ingestion and access (proposed: 30–45m) — Laura and Dev: can we make space next week?
- Ashley/Devon: please confirm the IdP and a target date for a dev/test S3 share.

Thanks — looking forward to the next step.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ashley Kim <ashley.kim@orionhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, Devon Park <devon.park@orionhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:08:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: OrionHealth SDK auth & model-routing runbook

Thanks Rishi — that aligns with what we talked about. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: the 100ms p95 is a soft goal for simple triage prompts. For discharge/summary we accept higher latency (up to 800ms p95) if accuracy increases.
- IdP: Okta (SAML) for console; for API auth we prefer short-lived service tokens and mTLS as an option.
- Data: we’ll provide an anonymized S3 bucket with one week of sample segments by next Friday (we’ll send details to your team).

Also — security will ask for a SOC2 snapshot and our procurement team will want the vendor questionnaire completed. Could you have those ready in parallel?

Finally, curious about routing: if you detect increased latency in US-East would Redwood automatically fail over to another model in-region or to another region? We need to avoid cross-region patient data movement.

Ashley
Ashley Kim
Director of Engineering, OrionHealth
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
To: Ashley Kim <ashley.kim@orionhealth.com>, Devon Park <devon.park@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 10:25:32 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: OrionHealth SDK auth & model-routing runbook

Ashley — great points. Answers inline + attached runbook + artifacts.

On latency / failover:
- Redwood policy model: routing is policy-driven and region-aware. You can set: 
  * region_strict = true (block cross-region routing) OR
  * region_strict = false (allow region fallback).
- For your case we recommend region_strict = true; within-region fallback chains are limited to compatible model variants that reside in US-East. That prevents cross-region data transfer.
- We’ll expose these as simple JSON policy objects in the Console and via SDK (example attached: orion-routing-policy-draft.csv).

On auth + compliance:
- SOC2 snapshot and vendor questionnaire: attaching SOC2-2025-summary.pdf (redacted) and our vendor questionnaire link in the drive.
- API flow: sample mTLS config in the SDK quickstart. We also support short-lived tokens minted by your STS and mapped to Redwood service accounts.

On embeddings + reranker:
- Upsert pipeline: we’ll provide a small ingestion lambda (example in the runbook) that reads S3 -> batches embeddings (512 dim) -> upserts to the index.
- Reranker: we recommend in-line reranker as a secondary call (same request context) so you can keep scoring local and avoid extra round trips. SDK will show how to call the reranker and pass back structured scores.

Attachments included:
- redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (code snippets: service account, mTLS, structured output handler)
- orion-routing-policy-draft.csv (policy examples: latency thresholds, cost tiers, fallback chains)
- redwood-runbook-v1.pdf (detailed runbook + ingestion checklist)

Proposed immediate schedule:
- Dev sync (30m): Monday 2026-07-20 11:00am ET — Laura & Dev to attend?
- Security handoff: I’ll route SOC2 + questionnaire to your security.

If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

— Rishi
From: Devon Park <devon.park@orionhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>, Ashley Kim <ashley.kim@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example.com>

Looks good — confirming the Monday slot (2026-07-20 11:00am ET works). I’ll drop the test S3 bucket info in a separate email to Rishi and Dev with read-only keys.

Quick note on data: security asked that the anonymization script be shared with the ingestion lambda so we can validate irreversibility. Can you include a short section in the runbook that describes the expected data schema and anonymization steps?

Also happy to take the initial routing CSV and iterate — I’ll add cost tiers on our side once I see Redwood’s suggested thresholds.

Thanks — Devon
